Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

The existing-remedy digests below are numbered [R1]…[RN]. There are 7 existing-remedy digests. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

remedy_content.text:
# Fake Release Discipline

Before reporting any task, migration, or release as complete, run its declared verification/check command and report the actual result plainly. Never say "done" or "fixed" while a known check is still failing.

structured_output.routing_rationale: Incident 11 is a plain premature-completion-claim: the agent said a migration was "complete" while the very checks meant to verify it were still failing. This is exactly the failure mode R2's existing global CLAUDE.md block ("Fake Release Discipline") already targets — run the declared verification command and report the actual result before claiming done. R1's skill covers the same territory at higher context cost. Per the cheapest-remedy-first rule, this stays a claude-md revision (not a new skill or hook): I'm broadening R2's wording from "release" to any task/migration/check, since the incident shows the pattern isn't limited to releases. No hook is proposed because there's no single mechanical gate across arbitrary "declared verification commands" without knowing the project's check-runner; a standing instruction is the cheapest fix that generalizes.
